transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

Based on your description, the most likely culprit is a failed Heating Element.

Here’s why:
• The drum turns → Motor and belt are working.
• Cold air blows → Fan and thermostat are likely working (since air is moving).
• No heat → The component responsible for generating heat has failed.

### 🔧 Part You Likely Need:
Beko Heating Element Assembly
(Also called the "heater coil" or "heating element kit")

⚠️ Important: Do not buy a generic universal part unless you’re sure it matches your model. Beko dryers use specific voltage (usually 230V in the UK/EU) and physical configurations.

---

### ✅ Steps to Confirm & Replace:

#### 1. Find Your Exact Model Number
• Look on the door frame, inside the door seal, or on the back of the dryer.
• Example format: `BWD...`, `BHV...`, etc. (e.g., `BWD84320`)
• Search online for:
  `"Beko [Your Model Number] heating element"`

#### 2. Safety First
• Unplug the dryer from the mains before any inspection or repair.
• Wait 15–30 minutes after unplugging (capacitors can hold charge).

#### 3. Quick Diagnostic Check (Optional but Recommended)
If you’re handy with a multimeter:
• Access the heating element (usually behind the rear panel or bottom panel).
• Disconnect it and test for continuity across its terminals.
• No continuity = Heating element is broken → Replace it.

#### 4. Replacement Cost & Effort
• Part cost: £15–£30 online (e.g., Spares2go, PartSelect, Amazon UK).
• Time: ~30–60 minutes if you follow a YouTube guide for your model.
• Difficulty: Moderate – requires removing panels and handling electrical connections safely.

---

### 🚨 Other Possible (But Less Likely) Causes:
If the heating element tests fine, consider:
1. Thermal Fuse/Thermistor – If blown, it cuts power to the heater for safety. Test for continuity.
2. Timer/Electronic Control Board – Rarely fails completely, but possible if no heat signal is sent.
3. Thermostat – If stuck open, it won’t allow current to reach the heating element.

---

### 💡 Recommendation:
1. Search for your model number + "heating element" on a reputable spare parts site.
2. Watch a YouTube tutorial for your specific Beko model before starting.
3. If you’re not comfortable with electrical repairs, hire a qualified appliance technician.

The DV7110 is a very common Beko model (often sold as part of the DV71 series). Since you don’t have a multimeter and can’t easily access the back label, here’s exactly what to do:

### 🔍 Step 1: Find the Full Model Number
The DV7110 is just the series name. The full model number (e.g., `BWD84320`, `DV7110G`, etc.) is on a sticker usually located:
• Inside the door frame
• On the top edge of the dryer (look up from below)
• Behind the lint filter cover

If you can’t see it, try this:
1. Pull the dryer out slightly (even an inch helps).
2. Shine a torch into the door gap or look at the top rim.
3. The full model will start with BWD, BHV, or similar, followed by numbers/letters.

### 🔧 Step 2: Heating Element Part Number for DV71 Series
For most Beko DV71 series dryers (including DV7110), the heating element is a standard part. Try searching for these exact terms on UK parts sites:
• "Beko DV7110 heating element"
• "BWD84320 heating element" (this is one of the most common model numbers in this series)

### 🛒 Where to Buy & Verify:
Go to these trusted UK spare parts websites and enter your full model number (once you find it):
1. Spares2go.com – Search "DV7110" → Look for "Heating Element Kit"
2. PartSelect.co.uk – Same search
3. Amazon UK – Search "Beko DV7110 heating element"

### ⚠️ Important Notes:
• The part usually includes the heating coil, thermal fuse, and sometimes a thermostat.
• Cost: ~£15–£25.
• If you can’t find the full model number, take a photo of the DV7110 label and show it to customer service at Spares2go or PartSelect – they can often identify the correct part from the series name alone.

### 🛠️ Replacement Tip:
Since you’re wedged in an alcove, consider this before buying:
• If replacing the heating element requires removing the dryer from the alcove, it may be easier to call a professional (cost ~£80–£120).
• If you can access the rear or bottom panel without moving the dryer, DIY is straightforward.

I cannot give you a single guaranteed part number for "DV7110" because that is a series name, not a specific model, and Beko uses different internal components across that range. Guessing could lead to buying the wrong part or creating a safety hazard.

However, I can answer your two direct questions based on standard Beko DV71 design:

### 1. Which part is it?
Given the heavily clogged vent, the most likely failed part is the Thermal Fuse (also called a Thermal Cut-out or High-Limit Thermostat).
• Why? A blocked vent causes overheating. The thermal fuse blows as a safety measure to cut power to the heater.
• Less likely but possible: The Heating Element itself may have failed due to age/overheating, but the thermal fuse is the primary suspect when ventilation was poor.

### 2. Can you replace it without pulling the dryer out?
Yes, in most Beko DV71 models, you can access and replace the thermal fuse without moving the dryer from its alcove.
• Access: The thermal fuse is typically located on the back panel or inside the drum housing, accessible by removing:
• The top panel (two screws at the back)
• Or the rear service panel (usually 4–6 screws)
• Location: It’s a small ceramic or metal component with two wires, mounted near the heater assembly or on the duct path.
• No meter needed? You can visually inspect it for breaks, but without a multimeter, you’re replacing it as a precautionary fix. If the new fuse blows immediately after replacement, the heating element or thermostat is also faulty.

### 🛠️ Next Steps:
1. Identify your exact model: Look inside the door frame, on the lint filter housing, or on the top edge of the dryer for a label starting with `BWD`, `BHV`, or similar (e.g., `BWD84320`).
2. Search for that full model + "thermal fuse" on Spares2go.com or PartSelect.co.uk.
3. Replace the thermal fuse using the guide above. If it fails again, replace the heating element too.

If you can’t find the full model number, I strongly recommend calling a qualified engineer (£80–£120) to avoid safety risks.
